description: Staggered arrangement that places each horizontal velocity component at the centre of a cell edge but directed tangential (parallel) to that edge, with mass-related quantities at the cell centre. It is the transpose of the C grid, in which the same points carry the component normal to the edge, and it represents vorticity rather than divergence on the compact single-grid-spacing stencil. The D grid is rarely used on its own and appears mainly as the second half of combined C-D or CD schemes, where the two arrangements are used in alternation to gain the advantages of both.
